summary: POC scoping call focused on security/compliance requirements for a 4-week pilot and benchmark plan. Customer requires SOC 2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML + SCIM, fine-grained RBAC, and audit log retention. Discussed workload sizing (peak 250 rps, 20M tokens/month), latency SLOs, and timeline for benchmark runs and pilot start.
transcript:
Header: 2025-01-17 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~48 minutes | Recording: cloud | Attendees: Emily Carter (Redwood AE), Marcus Huang (Redwood SE), Sofia Martinez (CTO - Hyperion), Liam O'Neill (Head Infra), Dr. Ananya Rao (Data Privacy), Omar Farouk (ML Eng), Grace Kim (PM)

Summary (auto): quick alignment on what security artifacts Hyperion needs, what Redwood can provide for a pilot, sizing numbers for the benchmark, and agreed next steps.

[00:00] Emily Carter: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick roll call — we can start with a 5-minute overview of the pilot goals then dive into security. Marcus will run the bench section.
[00:17] Sofia Martinez: Thanks, Emily. Our primary thing is to validate both security posture and the inference economics — we want to see cost per 1M tokens and latency under our P50/P95 targets. Also need to check integrations for SSO and audit capabilities.
[00:33] Marcus Huang: Great, we'll show the benchmark plan and the harness. Off the bat, can you confirm expected workload shape? That drives instance sizing and quantization profile.
[00:46] Omar Farouk: Sure. Typical profile: baseline 40-60 rps, peak bursts up to 250 rps for 20-30 minutes, average sequence length around 300 tokens, monthly token volume estimated ~20M tokens. We also have some multi-turn chat flows with KV cache hits approx 30%.
[01:05] Marcus Huang: Perfect, that helps. For the pilot we'll recommend a small dedicated pool with scaling headroom; for the benchmark we can emulate the burst and KV cache behaviour.
[01:21] Liam O'Neill: On security: primary checklist — SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 summary, SSO via SAML, SCIM for provisioning, RBAC with role separation, audit logs with 12 months retention, KMS integration for key control. Anything else?
[01:36] Emily Carter: That's the common enterprise ask. We'll send the SOC 2 report redacted, an ISO posture summary, and details on our KMS integrations. Note on private deployment options as well if you need on-prem or VPC private control plane.
[01:50] Dr. Ananya Rao: Data residency question — are logs or prompts stored outside the region by default? We need to make sure PHI-related prompts never leave EU infrastructure for a subset of customers.
[02:05] Marcus Huang: We have region pinning and data residency options for private/dedicated tiers. For hosted, we can pin to EU region, and for private we can ensure routing to on-prem. Also our KV cache is ephemeral unless you opt-in to retention.
[02:26] Sofia Martinez: For success criteria for the pilot: 1) latency P95 < 350ms for our standard prompt set, 2) throughput at 200 rps for 10-minute sustained windows without error rate >0.5%, 3) pass security checklist including SSO and audit log access, 4) cost estimate within X of our target (we gave an internal target).
[02:49] Grace Kim: And add quality regression — generation quality must not degrade more than 5% on our eval prompts (we'll send eval set).
[03:03] Marcus Huang: We'll run a baseline with the same eval set and report perplexity / Rouge-ish metrics and also human eval notes if you want.
[03:18] Liam O'Neill: How do you do RBAC? We want separate roles for infra admins, auditors, and application owners. Fine-grained access to models and keys.
[03:32] Emily Carter: RBAC is role-based with tenant-scoped roles. You can create custom roles and bind them to SAML groups via SCIM sync. Auditors can have read-only access to console logs and exportable audit logs.
[03:46] Omar Farouk: About audit logs: what's the retention policy and how are they exported? We might need syslog forwarding to our SIEM.
[03:55] Marcus Huang: Audit logs are kept for 12 months by default for enterprise, and we can push logs to your S3 or to syslog/Datadog — we support export hooks. We'll include a sample log schema in the security packet.
[04:12] Sofia Martinez: Any PCI or PHI specific compliance? We need to map to HIPAA controls even if you don't claim full attestation.
[04:21] Emily Carter: We don't claim HIPAA attestation in hosted mode by default; we can discuss Private deployment or BAAs for covered use cases. For pilot we'll provide controls mapping and our encryption at rest/in transit details.
[04:36] Marcus Huang: Back to benchmarks — we'll propose a 2-phase bench: Phase A synthetic latency/throughput with fixed prompt, Phase B with your eval corpus and multi-turn flows including KV cache and long sequence tests. We'll do cold start and warmed KV cache runs.
[04:54] Omar Farouk: Cold start behavior is important. Our traffic has a lot of cold tails for new users. What's warm-up time for model instances and how long until KV cache populates?
[05:08] Marcus Huang: Cold start varies by pod size and model; for a typical 8-GPU-ish pool we see cold latency 2-3x P50, but warmed pools keep P95 stable. KV cache warm-up depends on prefix reuse — we'll simulate that.
[05:25] Grace Kim: Timeline question — we want pilot to start first week of Feb and run four weeks. Is that workable?
[05:33] Emily Carter: Yes, works if we get your data slices and SSO metadata this week for pre-work. We'll aim to run bench the week of Jan 27, and then pilot start Feb 3.
[05:46] Sofia Martinez: Ok. On SSO: we use Okta primarily. We need SAML integration + SCIM provisioning and have a test org. We'll share metadata. Also want to confirm JIT provisioning?
[05:59] Emily Carter: We support SCIM for provisioning and de-provisioning. JIT can be arranged for some flows but SCIM is preferred for enterprise.
[06:10] Liam O'Neill: Encryption keys — can we bring our own key (BYOK) for any persisted artifacts? We want HSM-backed keys for long-term secrets.
[06:20] Marcus Huang: For enterprise/dedicated we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations. We'll include a diagram on what is encrypted with customer keys versus platform keys.
[06:32] Dr. Ananya Rao: Audit record access — can we blind redact prompts in logs or keep prompt text out of logs for privacy?
[06:41] Emily Carter: You can configure logging levels; we can redact prompt content in logs and only retain metadata (request id, model, latency). For pilot we'll provide an optioned log export.
[06:54] Omar Farouk: One more technical: do you have inference quantization options? We run some models quantized int8 to save cost but want to check quality impact.
[07:04] Marcus Huang: Yes, we support quantized variants and our Optimize tool recommends quant profiles per workload. The bench will include quality delta comparisons across FP16 and int8-like profiles.
[07:17] Sofia Martinez: On the security docs, we need: SOC 2 Type II, ISO27001 summary, network diagram, encryption + KMS details, incident response playbook, and the audit log schema.
[07:30] Emily Carter: We'll package that. Expect redacted SOC 2 within 48 hours and an ISO posture doc. Marcus will attach the log schema and bench plan.
[07:40] Grace Kim: For success criteria — can we make it explicit in the pilot charter? We'll send a one-pager with target metrics and gating criteria.
[07:49] Emily Carter: Yes, we'll use that to define pass/fail for the pilot.
[07:56] Marcus Huang: Quick question on environment: do you want hosted dedicated or private for the pilot? It changes setup and SOC docs we provide.
[08:04] Liam O'Neill: Prefer dedicated reserved capacity in EU region for pilot. Not full on-prem, but strict networking rules and private control plane access.
[08:13] Marcus Huang: Dedicated is a good middle ground — we can do VPC peering and private endpoints. We'll provide a network checklist.
[08:22] Sofia Martinez: Bench specifics — P50 target around 120-150ms for short prompts, P95 < 350ms. Error budget <0.5% and stability across 10-minute sustained 200 rps windows. Also cost per token within red-team threshold.
[08:40] Marcus Huang: We'll capture metrics: p50/p95 latency, error rate, cost per 1k tokens, and quality regressions on your eval set. We'll attach the runbook.
[08:50] Omar Farouk: How do you instrument traces? We want distributed tracing correlation ids.
[08:56] Marcus Huang: We expose request ids and have tracing hooks; you can push traces to your tracing backend or we can push export. We'll include correlation guidance.
[09:07] Dr. Ananya Rao: About retention — do we have legal hold options on logs if an audit arises?
[09:14] Emily Carter: Yes, we have legal hold workflows for enterprise accounts; we'll include the process and SLAs.
[09:23] Grace Kim: Any blockers from Redwood's side?
[09:26] Emily Carter: Nothing blocking — main dependency is Hyperion providing eval set, SSO metadata, and traffic profile. Then we run bench week of Jan 27 and pilot starts Feb 3.
[09:38] Sofia Martinez: Sounds good. Regarding pricing for pilot — can we get an estimated cost for the four-week reserved capacity?
[09:45] Emily Carter: We'll send a proposed pilot pricing sheet as part of the next email. It will include committed capacity estimate and an overage rate.
[09:54] Omar Farouk: For the bench harness — can you run with our model snapshots or only Redwood-curated models? We sometimes have fine-tuned weights.
[10:02] Marcus Huang: We can run your fine-tuned model if it's compatible with the runtime and licensing; for pilot we can bring it into a private pool. We'll need a model artifact package and the runtime config.
[10:18] Liam O'Neill: Licensing — need assurances on IP and ephemeral model storage.
[10:24] Emily Carter: We'll include contractual language in the pilot agreement: model artifacts are isolated and deleted after pilot unless you opt to keep.
[10:33] Grace Kim: OK, wrap up then next steps.
[10:36] Emily Carter: Recap — Redwood to share SOC2 & ISO summary, bench harness and run plan, pilot pricing, and network checklist. Hyperion to share eval set, traffic profile, and Okta metadata. Action items noted. We'll target bench week of Jan 27 and pilot start Feb 3 for 4 weeks.
[10:58] Sofia Martinez: Cool, thanks. Looking forward to the packet.
[11:02] Emily Carter: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up by EOD with links.

(Transcript contains occasional transcription errors, e.g., 'KV cash' vs KV cache, 'SOC two' vs SOC 2.)
